ARABIC LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sound does the Arabic letter ث make? (1 mark)
   A. th as in think
   B. j as in jug
   C. d as in dog
   D. kh, a throat sound like the ch in loch

2. How do you read the syllable تِ? (1 mark)
   A. si
   B. laa
   C. nii
   D. ti

3. Which letters can make a vowel long? (1 mark)
   A. baa, taa and thaa
   B. alif, waaw and yaa
   C. siin, shiin and Saad
   D. laam, miim and nuun

4. How do you read the syllable نُ? (1 mark)
   A. bi
   B. nu
   C. la
   D. ni

5. Which is the correct blend of the syllables a + bun? (1 mark)
   A. buna
   B. bana
   C. nuba
   D. abun

6. How is the Arabic word أَخٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. akh
   B. usra
   C. khaal
   D. ʿamma

7. In a passage about the home, which of these is a theme word? (1 mark)
   A. kursii (chair)
   B. marhaban
   C. al-ahad
   D. shukran

8. What does the Arabic sentence فِي الْمَطْبَخِ طَاوِلَةٌ وَكُرْسِيٌّ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The house is big.
   B. In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   C. On the table there is a cup.
   D. This is my room.

9. How is the Arabic word الْجُمُعَةُ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. al-yawm
   B. usbuuʿ
   C. al-ithnayn
   D. al-jumuʿa

10. What does the word ghadan mean? (1 mark)
   A. yesterday
   B. week
   C. tomorrow
   D. today

11. Which Arabic sentence means "This is a party." (1 mark)
   A. الْأَصْدِقَاءُ فِي الْحَفْلَةِ
   B. فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ بَالُونٌ
   C. هَذِهِ حَفْلَةٌ
   D. عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كَعْكَةٌ

12. Which question word means 'who'? (1 mark)
   A. limaadhaa
   B. ayna
   C. man
   D. kam

13. Which Arabic word means "vegetables"? (1 mark)
   A. خُضَارٌ
   B. مَوْزٌ
   C. لَحْمٌ
   D. حَلِيبٌ

14. What does the Arabic sentence أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I like food.
   B. The juice is cold.
   C. Water is useful (good for you).
   D. The fish is delicious.

15. How is the Arabic word قَدَمٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. katif
   B. qadam
   C. udhun
   D. sinn

16. How is the Arabic word أَنْفٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. qalb
   B. ʿayn
   C. fam
   D. anf

17. What is rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. Words or lines that end with the same sound
   B. A kind of picture
   C. A long word
   D. A number

18. What does the Arabic sentence الشَّمْسُ فِي السَّمَاءِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. And the rain is from the sky.
   B. How beautiful the environment is!
   C. In the room there is a bed.
   D. The sun is in the sky.

19. What is a thematic word? (1 mark)
   A. A word in English
   B. A number
   C. A very long word
   D. A word that belongs to the theme of a text

20. How does a reading circle work? (1 mark)
   A. Everyone reads silently
   B. One learner reads for the whole hour
   C. Each learner takes a turn to read aloud
   D. Only the teacher reads

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Name three verbal cues and say how each one helps the listener. (3 marks) (3 marks)

22. Describe how to make a vocabulary bank of words about the home. (3 marks) (3 marks)

23. Translate into English: fii l-matbakhi taawila wa kursii. (2 marks) (2 marks)

24. Give three items from a peer review checklist for reading aloud. (3 marks) (3 marks)

25. Explain how a spelling bee is played. (3 marks) (3 marks)

26. Translate into English: jismii qawiyy (2 marks)

27. Say what a vocabulary bank is and how you can make one from a poem. (3 marks) (3 marks)

28. Translate into English: fawqa t-taawilati baaluun (2 marks)

29. Translate into English: lii yadaani (2 marks)

30. Translate into English: jaddii kabiir (2 marks)

31. Translate into English: usaaʿidu ummii yawma s-sabt. (2 marks) (2 marks)

32. Give three differences between the Arabic and the English alphabets. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — th as in think
   The letter ث makes the sound th as in think.

2. D — ti
   تِ is read ti.

3. B — alif, waaw and yaa
   Alif, waaw and yaa lengthen a matching short vowel.

4. B — nu
   نُ is read nu.

5. D — abun
   The syllables are read in order: a then bun gives abun (father).

6. A — akh
   أَخٌ is read akh and means brother.

7. A — kursii (chair)
   A theme word belongs to the topic. A chair is found in the home.

8. B — In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   فِي الْمَطْبَخِ طَاوِلَةٌ وَكُرْسِيٌّ (fii l-matbakhi taawila wa kursii) means: In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.

9. D — al-jumuʿa
   الْجُمُعَةُ is read al-jumuʿa and means Friday.

10. C — tomorrow
   ghadan means tomorrow. amsi means yesterday.

11. C — هَذِهِ حَفْلَةٌ
   هَذِهِ حَفْلَةٌ (haadhihi hafla) means: This is a party.

12. C — man
   man means who. ayna means where, kam means how many and limaadhaa means why.

13. A — خُضَارٌ
   خُضَارٌ (khudaar) means vegetables.

14. A — I like food.
   أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ (uhibbu T-taʿaam) means: I like food.

15. B — qadam
   قَدَمٌ is read qadam and means foot.

16. D — anf
   أَنْفٌ is read anf and means nose.

17. A — Words or lines that end with the same sound
   Rhyme is when words or lines end with the same sound.

18. D — The sun is in the sky.
   الشَّمْسُ فِي السَّمَاءِ (ash-shamsu fii s-samaa'i) means: The sun is in the sky.

19. D — A word that belongs to the theme of a text
   Thematic words belong to the main topic of a text.

20. C — Each learner takes a turn to read aloud
   In a reading circle each learner reads in turn.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Intonation shows questions and statements; speed shows importance or excitement; tonal variation shows feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cue with its use.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write each Arabic word on a card with a picture; write the sound and meaning on the back; keep the cards in a box or on a chart and use them to practise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Every word read correctly; steady pace; voice rises for questions; pauses at commas; voice shows feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid item.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Teams take turns; a learner says the Arabic word and spells it by naming the letters; correct spelling earns a point.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for teams, 1 mark for spelling by letter names and 1 mark for scoring.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: My body is strong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: A vocabulary bank keeps new words for later. Pick out the words from the poem and write each with its sound, meaning and a picture on cards.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 2 marks for the method.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Above the table there is a balloon.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have two hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: My grandfather is old (big in age).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: I help my mother on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'I help my mother' and 1 mark for 'on Saturday'.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Arabic is read from right to left; it has no capital letters; letters join and change shape; it uses marks for short vowels; it has sounds like ʿayn and Haa that English does not have.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference, up to 3.
